items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Comments are good at the module level and on tricky spots (opq/volatile hack). But names are cryptic all over: `k`, `c`, `f`, `fs`, `fsz`, `f2s`, `cps`, `opq`, `ilo/ihi`, `yc0/uc0`. FFmpeg-style single letters (B, C, d, dd, ddd) also appear in the filter logic.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: simd.zig is about 70KB and main.zig/kernels.zig are each over 20KB, far past 500 lines. filter.init ports FFmpeg's huge initFilter as one function, likely over 100 lines. There is global mutable `var zero_opaque` with a volatile hack, and code was patched by regex rename (pairOld left behind).

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Uses errdefer/defer and a filters_ok flag for cleanup, and create returns NULL on error.Unsupported for filters of 256+ taps. Magic constants are everywhere, though (64<<12, >>19, 4096, 0.002, 54-lg), and the valgrind run was not finished.

items.name: Geometry, stride and tail handling
items.name_zh: 几何尺寸、步长与尾部处理
items.evidence: Scalar tails are present (vInterleavedTail). A 1044-case odd-size sweep passed, and NULL is returned for the cascade case. Valgrind did not cover every case, and the fixed [512][*]const i16 arrays rest on a size assumption. Stride handling cannot be fully verified from what is shown.

items.name: ABI and build-target conformance
items.name_zh: ABI 与构建目标符合要求
items.evidence: build.zig pins the x86_64_v3 cpu_model. The final check showed only the three API functions exported, no ff_ symbols and no zmm (AVX-512) instructions, and the code is single-threaded.
